attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6 found `_round.id = INV-R6.1` sitting beside an `implementation` field still describing R5.2's support-edge work, and a `note` describing R5.2's count drift, with every gate green. THE SIXTH LAYER at which this artifact has recorded `two descriptions of one state drift`, and the first at which it committed the error in the header that names the round. The usual answer here is render-and-compare (MOS-DERIVED-EQ) and it is the wrong one: there is no reason for the ledger to hold a second account of a transition at all, and derived equality would only make the duplicate harder to see. The prose moved into mosaic/receipts/INV-R6.2.json where the transition is described once.
attrs.statement: The ledger's `_round` header carries an id, a date and a reference to its receipt. It may not carry a second account of the transition.
